newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria and Slovenia sign free trade agreement.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria and Slovenia sign free trade agreement.

text.p: Bulgaria and Slovenia signed a free trade agreement on Friday, which is expected to boost bilateral trade and help Bulgaria join the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA).
"The free trade agreement that has been signed today comes as a result of both countries' desire to develop their trade relations," Bulgaria's Trade Minister Atanas Paparizov told a news conference.
He said the agreement was a new step on the way to Bulgarian membership of CEFTA. Earlier this year, Bulgaria concluded free trade agreements with the Czech Republic and Slovakia.
"With the signing of this agreement we are expecting trade between both countries to rise significantly," said Slovenian Economic Relations and Development Minister Janko Dezelak.
He said Slovenia, which is to chair CEFTA in 1997, would support the conclusion of procedures to admit Bulgaria as a member.
Under the agreement, due to come into force in January 1997, duties on certain Slovenian and Bulgarian goods will be abolished by the year 2000.
According to the scheme, duties on industrial goods are to be reduced by 60 to 80 percent in 1997, and be fully abolished in 1998 and 1999.

Trade between the two countries has recorded a drop this year, mainly due to difficulties in Bulgaria, which is currently in a deep economic crisis and is mulling the introduction of a currency board to stabilise its collapsing financial sector.
Bulgarian imports from Slovenia mainly consist of cars, drugs, chemicals and aluminium products. Exports include oil, wood products, vegetables and copper.
In the first nine months of this year, Bulgarian imports from Slovenia reached $6.8 million, a 30 percent drop on the same period of 1995, while exports fell by 86.7 percent to $2.88 million.
This week Bulgaria's trade ministry reported a $1 billion drop in total industrial exports in the first half of 1996 against the same period last year.
